# One refinement has no red of its own, and the record says so

The tdd gate refused a record citing record 4 as the red for two slices. It is right: two slices
sharing a red are one slice described twice.

What actually happened: record 4 was one red covering the environment-value rule and the
marketplace-host lint together, both written in the same file, and record 5 was the green for both.
Then running the lint on this repository found its own test file and the compiled bytecode beside it,
so the lint gained a per-line marker and stopped scanning compiled files. That refinement was written
and checked outside the harness, so it has no recorded red; record 6 is its green.

The tdd record therefore carries two slices, not three, and this note is where the refinement is
accounted for. Inventing a red for it after the fact would be worse than saying it plainly, and the
rule SEEN-089 added exists precisely so that a red cannot be manufactured to suit a record.
